page: Microsoft Azure E4as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor operating at up to 3.35 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 4 vCPUs sourced from 2 physical cores utilizing simultaneous multithreading. It is configured with 32 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The virtual machine includes 69 GB of local SSD temporary storage, while hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not present. Supported instruction set extensions include AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI, while AVX-512 extensions are absent.

Performance metrics show strong single-core CPU throughput, with stress-ng single-core benchmarks scoring in the top 25 percentile. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks such as PassMark CPU and multi-threaded stress-ng place in the bottom 25 percentile, reflecting the 4 vCPU constraint. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 20.8 GB/sec and write bandwidth measures 11.87 GB/sec, placing in the bottom 10 percentile for memory throughput. Redis operations reach 3.64 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 4.11 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server eliminates the necessity to purchase surplus compute cores when an application primarily demands memory capacity. The included 69 GB local SSD provides integrated fast storage for scratch data, caching, or swap files without external volume overhead. Tradeoffs include moderate memory bandwidth and limited parallel processing capability. Best-fit workloads include relational database management systems, in-memory caching tiers such as Redis, business intelligence processing, and general back-end microservices requiring elevated RAM allocations.
description: Microsoft Azure E4as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7452 processor running at 3.35 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with multithreading, coupled with 32 GB of RAM and 69 GB of local SSD temporary storage. With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the instance prioritizes memory capacity over multi-threaded compute density. Hardware telemetry indicates strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng tests, alongside moderate compression throughput and single-core Geekbench ratings. However, multi-core throughput and uncached memory bandwidth remain constrained due to the 4 vCPU limit and architectural bandwidth bottlenecks. The bundled local SSD provides rapid scratch space for caching and temporary operational data. This configuration suits memory-intensive enterprise tasks such as mid-sized relational database systems, in-memory caching tiers, small Redis deployments, and data transformation jobs that require substantial memory footprint without massive parallel compute capacity.

AMD EPYC 7452 processor delivering up to 3.35 GHz clock frequency
